column1: # claim-ledger.tsv — one row per durable claim: id <TAB> command <TAB> expect <TAB> exit <TAB> timeout <TAB> note
# `expect` is an ERE matched against the LAST non-empty line of the command's
# combined stdout+stderr; the exit code must equal the fifth column. Both must
# hold. Rows are reviewed, committed, and refused (POLICY, exit 2) if they are
# not a single simple command (allowlisted first token, no metacharacters, no
# denied verb) — see corpus/claim-ledger.sh header §Command safety.
# R11-06 carries exit 1 on purpose: the recorded baseline of the transcript
# gate IS a firing gate (2 `xai-` prose-collision HITs, credential tripwires
# empty). A change in that line is a host-state event to re-baseline, not a
# Count rows (R11-10/11, and the `(N cases)` expectations) exist because three
# committed docs carried stale numbers for these same quantities (README said
# 20 state-shape rows and a 14-case census selftest; PROVINCE said 21 rows) —
# a number a doc cites is a claim, so it belongs here.

Pre-move: no such file existed — ownership was prose in three places, and one of them cited `kake-shokunin/SKILL.md:104-107` for a claim that lives at `:161`

the gate's own proof on a scratch tree: every rule R1-R11 has at least one failing-input case (FOREIGN, ORPHAN, UNKNOWN-OWNER x2 (undeclared and self-declared), BAD-VALUE, BAD-ROW x7 incl. an 8th column and a duplicate census row, OWNER-MISMATCH, OVERCLAIM both directions, NOT-A-FILE, STALE-BASIS, BASIS-ESCAPE x2, FOREIGN-SCAN, ESCAPE x2, INBOUND, UNVERIFIED x2, ENUM-CLASH x3, OWN-UNLISTED x2), plus CLEAN, the count pins, the map view from a foreign cwd, a bootstrap failure exiting 2 with a SETUP line, an absent asset row named `ADJACENCY_ASSET_ABSENT` vs a runtime row abstaining, and a missing data file exiting 2. The tree is rebuilt from scratch for every case (leaking fixtures produced false FAILs in the first revisions). Case count pinned: 28 -> 29 -> 30 -> 31 -> 36 -> 41 -> 42 -> 43 during landing

the mutation set runs against the SHIPPED data + census (mktemp copies, repo never written): a basis that resolves but points at the wrong lines (the `README.md:76` class, sed'd on the real kake citation), a census row in another lane's tree, a contested row drifted to a claim it may not make, a `# scan` over a shared dir, and a prefix crept over a directory the data itself declares unscanned. Nine mutations, all caught: the stale basis, a foreign census row, a drifted claim, a `# scan` over a shared dir, two prefix-creep variants (over a `# no-enumerate` dir and over a declared ancestor), an `# own` prefix over an undeclared tree, `..` traversal in a basis, and a clean-looking `lane:` citation whose lane root is a symlink out of the lane tree. Two earlier "known uncaught" instances were CLOSED rather than recorded: `# own $HOME/.local/bin` (105 foreign children, silent) is now `ENUM-CLASH` via R10's own-vs-no-enumerate clause, and `# own $HOME/projects` is now `OWN-UNLISTED` via R11. Run 1 of this mode caught its own first defect: both data files end WITHOUT a trailing newline, so a naive append merged the mutation into the last row and three mutations silently no-opped; run 2 caught a second: `mutate_case` did not count failures, so a summary line read PASS while printing FAIL

the data file declares 5 owned prefixes (config/the-janitor, bin/the-janitor, bin/tac-check, state/the-janitor, state/tac). The pattern is `+.HOME/` rather than `'^# own'` because the file's own prose lines also start with `# own` (a naive count returns 9 — this row is exactly the class it pins). Outside check: the gate computes the prefix count from the same file it partitions, so this row counts the data against nothing else — dropping a prefix leaves its census rows uncovered (FOREIGN) only if the census rows are still there, but a prefix deleted together with its rows would need this row to notice

the data file carries 4 group rows (opencode / chrome-profile / NativeMessagingHosts / agents-AGENTS.md) covering the 8 census rows outside the owned prefixes. `groups=4` in R16-01 is read from this file by the gate; this row is the outside count

8 directories are declared deliberately unscanned ($HOME/.local/bin, $HOME/.config/opencode, $HOME/.agents, the chrome-profile subtree) — the directive the census's ownership reasoning used to be a comment about. R10 gives it teeth: the dir must be a census row or an ancestor of one, must not be a `# scan` dir, and must not sit inside an `# own` prefix (that last clause is reviewer D2, which found `# own $HOME/.local/bin` passing CLEAN while covering 103 unclaimed children; declaring the four ancestors is what makes the same creep over `$HOME/.local/state` — 13 unclaimed live children — fire as ENUM-CLASH)
